style: An oil painting in colour of 1893 matching the first reference image exactly: the same dark vaulted gunsmith's shop, the same walnut and brass, the same cool shafts of window light through dusty air, deep shadow, strong value contrast. Loose visible brushstrokes, thick impasto in the lights, soft lost edges. No text, signature or border.

beats.text: Shot: close, no people. A tall glass-fronted walnut cabinet in a London gunsmith's shop, 1893: a row of new Winchester lever-action repeating rifles standing upright, blued steel barrels and brass receivers, a shaft of window light falling across them.

Shot: close, no people. A gunsmith's counter in 1893: a Winchester lever-action rifle laid on green baize, open pasteboard boxes of brass cartridges spilling a few rounds, a brass oil can and a cleaning rod, a cold line of daylight on the brass.

Shot: close, no people. A low glass display case in a gunsmith's shop, 1893: Webley revolvers, a pair of hunting knives in leather sheaths and a brace of pistols on dark velvet, reflections of a tall arched window on the glass.

Shot: close. Only a man's hands in shirt cuffs working the lever of a Winchester rifle at a gunsmith's counter, 1893, the rifle's action open, brass gleaming in a shaft of light, the shop dark behind.
